seventh and eighth graders (1) ... traditional costumes from different provinces. I wore a traditional Baju Bodo
from South Sulawesi, while Pipit wore a Minangkabau costume with a horn-shaped headdress (Tingkuluak).
First, we gathered at the school yard at 07.30 a.m.
Next, the marching band led the parade along Jalan

Minangkabau costume. Keep shining and preserving our Indonesian culture! Best wishes, Monita."

Kiri: Siswa SMP Merdeka berlomba Makan Kerupuk, Balap Kelereng dalam sendok, dan Balap Bakiak beregu (Unit 1).

Last year, SMP Merdeka celebrated Indonesia’s 78th Independence Day with various traditional games in the
schoolyard. Each class sent representatives to compete in the Kerupuk Race, Marble-in-Spoon Race, Tan-
dem Clogs (Bakiak) Race, and Sack Race.
First, Andre joined the Kerupuk Race. His hands were tied behind his back while he jumped to bite a cracker
hanging on a string. He ate his cracker very fast and won second place! Next, Monita participated in the
Marble-in-Spoon Race. She walked carefully while holding a spoon with a glass marble in her mouth. Halfway
to the finish line, the wind blew strongly, but her marble (9) ... fall to the ground. She finished first!
After that, Galang, Made, and Riko joined the three-person Bakiak Race. At the start, they lost their balance
and almost fell because they did not step at the same time. Then, Galang shouted, "Left, right, left, right!" to
synchronize their footsteps. Working together in harmony, they overtook two other teams and crossed the finish
line first!
teks_soal: Based on Gambar 1.2 and the text, what is the main rule of the Kerupuk Race?
pembahasan: Jawaban yang tepat adalah B (Participants must eat a hanging cracker with their hands behind their backs). Sesuai fakta dan informasi kunci yang termuat pada stimulus bacaan serta penerapan kaidah kebahasaan Kurikulum Merdeka Fase D.

opsi_jawaban.label: B

opsi_jawaban.label: C
opsi_jawaban.teks: Participants must walk on wooden tandem clogs

opsi_jawaban.label: D
opsi_jawaban.teks: Participants must carry a marble on a spoon

Last year, SMP Merdeka celebrated Indonesia’s 78th Independence Day with various traditional games in the
schoolyard. Each class sent representatives to compete in the Kerupuk Race, Marble-in-Spoon Race, Tan-
dem Clogs (Bakiak) Race, and Sack Race.
First, Andre joined the Kerupuk Race. His hands were tied behind his back while he jumped to bite a cracker
hanging on a string. He ate his cracker very fast and won second place! Next, Monita participated in the
Marble-in-Spoon Race. She walked carefully while holding a spoon with a glass marble in her mouth. Halfway
to the finish line, the wind blew strongly, but her marble (9) ... fall to the ground. She finished first!
After that, Galang, Made, and Riko joined the three-person Bakiak Race. At the start, they lost their balance
and almost fell because they did not step at the same time. Then, Galang shouted, "Left, right, left, right!" to
synchronize their footsteps. Working together in harmony, they overtook two other teams and crossed the finish
line first!

Goal: How to Save Electrical Energy in Your Bedroom Every Day
Why It Matters: Generating electricity mostly burns fossil fuels, which produces carbon dioxide emissions.
Saving electricity at home reduces carbon emissions and lowers your family’s monthly electricity bill!
Steps:
1. First, open your bedroom curtains and windows in the morning so natural sunlight and fresh air enter the
room.
2. Second, turn off the study lamp and ceiling light as soon as the room is bright enough.
3. Next, unplug your smartphone charger, laptop adapter, and fan plug from the wall socket when they are not
in use (because plugged-in chargers still consume "vampire power" or standby electricity!).
4. Then, set your air conditioner (AC) to an eco-friendly temperature (24◦C −26◦C) or use a low-wattage fan,
and turn it off 30 minutes before leaving the room.
5. Finally, always switch off all lights and electronics before leaving your bedroom (as shown on the right of
Gambar 3.2)!

stimulus_bacaan:
Last Sunday morning, a group of junior high school volunteers in Banyuwangi conducted a coastal cleanup at
Muncar Beach after a heavy storm the night before. While they were collecting plastic bottles and styrofoam
along the shoreline, Galang spotted a young green sea turtle (Chelonia mydas) struggling near the rocks. Its
front flipper was tightly entangled in a discarded nylon fishing net and plastic six-pack rings. Because of the
tight plastic entanglement, the turtle could not swim back to the ocean. Immediately, the team leader called
a local marine conservation officer. Using safety scissors, they carefully cut away the plastic net, cleaned the
turtle’s flipper, and released it safely into the sea. That afternoon, the volunteers collected 45 sacks of plastic
waste so that no other marine animals would be harmed.
teks_soal: [Tata Bahasa Kontekstual: Cause & Effect (because vs because of)] Why does the writer use "Because of" instead of "Because" in the sentence "Because of the tight plastic entanglement, the turtle could not swim back to the ocean"?
pembahasan: Jawaban yang tepat adalah A (Because "the tight plastic entanglement" is a Noun Phrase without a finite verb, not a full S + V clause.). Penjelasan: Because of + Noun Phrase.

opsi_jawaban.label: A
opsi_jawaban.teks: Because "the tight plastic entanglement" is a Noun Phrase without a finite verb, not a full S + V clause.

opsi_jawaban.label: B
opsi_jawaban.teks: Because the sentence is in the Simple Future Tense.

opsi_jawaban.label: C
opsi_jawaban.teks: Because "Because of" can only be used at the end of a question.

opsi_jawaban.label: D
opsi_jawaban.teks: Because the sea turtle is an uncountable noun.
